To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

anti‐CD34 is a more sensitive endothelial marker than anti‐vWf in prostate carcinoma, that the two investigated methods of microvascular quantification can be used interchangeably, and that high microvascular scores in prostate carcinoma may indicate poor prognosis.

anti‐CD34 antibody staining is superior to anti‐vWF antibody staining for the detection of microvessels and that both the grid method and the Chalkley method are useful for quantification of microvessles.
anti‐CD34 is a more sensitive marker of endothelial cells than anti‐vWf, and that the Chalkley count is a more sensitive method of quantification than the MVD.

the study of the microvascular system in prostate carcinoma.

anti‐CD34 is superior to vWF as a microvascular marker in prostate carcinoma, whereas MVD and Chalkley count methods can be used interchangeably.
the anti‐CD 34 antibodies are superior to the anti‐vWF in prostate cancer, and that the MVD is the best method for quantification of microvessels.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CD34 is a good antibody to stain microvasculature in prostate carcinoma, that Chalkley counts are compatible with MVD in this setting, and that high microvascular density may indicate poor prognosis in prostate cancer.
CD34‐positive vascular scores are superior to von Willebrand factor‐positive scores in prostate carcinoma, but the prognostic value of the vascular scores remains to be established.
anti‐CD34 is the best antibody for staining microvessels and the Chalkley method for evaluating microvascular density.

CD34 staining is more sensitive in the detection of microvessels compared to vWF staining.
CD34 antibodies are a better marker of microvessels, as compared to the vWF antibody, and the Chalkley method is better for counting microvessels.
